name: Richard Hayne
sec_insider_companies: URBAN OUTFITTERS INC (URBN) - CEO & Chairman of the Board
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Former hippie Richard Hayne opened his first apparel shop in the mid 1970s, near the University of Pennsylvania, with only $4,000.
Today, Urban Outfitters is a nationwide chain with more than 200 locations and over $5 billion in revenue.
Hayne took Urban Outfitters public in 1993 and owns nearly a quarter of the company with his wife.
Hayne became the company's CEO in 2012 after former CEO Glen Senk left to run New York-based jeweler and watchmaker David Yurman.
His firm has been at the center of controversy over the years when its products have offended the LGBT community, Navajos, Irish Americans and Jews.
forbes_facts: Hayne owns the 700-acre Doe Run Dairy farm in Pennsylvania, which produces cheese.
In 1969, after graduating with a degree in anthropology from Lehigh University, Hayne did a stint volunteering with Inuit in Alaska.

name: Timothy Springer
sec_insider_companies: Tectonic Therapeutic, Inc. (TECX) - Director,TenPercentOwner; Cartesian Therapeutics, Inc. (RNAC) - Director,TenPercentOwner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Timothy Springer is an immunologist and professor of biological chemistry and molecular pharmacology at Harvard Medical School.
He was a founding investor in publicly traded biotech outfit Moderna, investing about $5 million in 2010; he now owns an estimated 3% of the firm's shares.
Springer also owns shares of three smaller publicly traded biotech firms: Cartesian Therapeutics, Scholar Rock and Tectonic Therapeutic.
He first started teaching at Harvard in 1977 as an assistant professor.
In 1993, he founded biotech firm LeukoSite and took it public in 1998; the next year, he sold it to Millennium Therapeutics for $635 million.
forbes_facts: In 2017, Springer established the Institute for Protein Innovation, an independent nonprofit focused on researching proteins, with an initial grant of $10 million.
Springer bikes to work from his home in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts.

name: Raamdeo Agrawal
name_chinese: 拉姆德夫·兰戈帕尔·阿加瓦尔
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2016-2019)
forbes_bio: Raamdeo Agrawal cofounded Motilal Oswal Financial Services as a small securities firm with his pal Motilal Oswal in 1987.
The company now offers a range of services including investment banking and mutual funds.
Agrawal grew up in a village in Chattisgarh in central India and came to Mumbai for his accountancy studies.
In 2023, Agrawal made a pledge to donate 5% of his stake in Motilal Oswal to philanthropic causes, such as education, health and rural upliftment.
forbes_facts: Agrawal and Oswal lived in the same hostel in Mumbai while studying accountancy but became friends much later.
An ardent Warren Buffet fan, he has been attending Berkshire Hathaway's annual general meetings since 1995.

name: Yasuhiro Fukushima
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2000-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Yasuhiro Fukushima founded gaming software firm Enix, which merged with rival Square in 2003 to become Square Enix.
The Tokyo-listed company made its mark with its Final Fantasy franchise and its Dragon Quest series.
He currently serves as the honorary chairman of Square Enix Holdings.

name: Remi Dassault
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Remi Dassault is the son of Olivier Dassault, an heir to the Dassault aerospace and software fortune.
Olivier Dassault's grandfather founded Dassault Aviation, a French aerospace company that started out making propellers in World War I.
His father Olivier, a prominent French politician who served as a representative in France's National Assembly, died in a helicopter crash in 2021.
The Dassault family also own the country's daily newspaper Le Figaro, several vineyards and a private aeronautic company.
forbes_facts: His sister Helena is also a billionaire.

name: Acharya Balkrishna
name_chinese: 阿查里亚·巴拉克拉希纳
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun India (2018-2022)
forbes_bio: Acharya Balkrishna derives his fortune from consumer goods giant Patanjali  Ayurved.
Balkrishna owns the bulk of the privately held company, which he cofounded with politically well-connected yoga guru Baba Ramdev.
Patanjali sells everything from herbal toothpastes and cosmetics to noodles and jams.
To push online sales, Patanjali has agreements with several e-commerce giants, such as Amazon and BigBasket.
Edible oils maker Ruchi Soya, which he acquired in 2019, was renamed as Patanjali Foods and he was installed as chairman.
forbes_facts: Balkrishna is often dressed in an all-white traditional dhoti.
In 2024, he apologised to India's Supreme Court for Patanjali's ads that allegedly make misleading claims about the medicinal benefits of its products.

name: Enrique Coppel Luken
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Enrique Coppel Luken and his four brothers own Grupo Coppel, a retail and banking business in Mexico with over $8 billion in sales.
Their father and grandfather founded the first shop in Sinaloa, where they sold radios and watches.
The group's retail arm has grown from a single shop in 1941 to over 1,700 stores across Mexico.
The stores are known for providing credit to customers, allowing them to finance their purchases over multiple payments.
Enrique was chairman and CEO until Agustín, the youngest of the bunch, took over in 2008.
forbes_facts: The brothers also have two sisters who don't have active roles in the business.

name: Fred Ehrsam
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Fred Ehrsam founded cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase in 2012 with Brian Armstrong. It has since grown into the largest U.S. crypto brokerage.
Ehrsam left the company in 2017 but remains on the board and still owns about 4% of its stock; Coinbase went public in 2021.
In 2018, he cofounded Paradigm, a cryptocurrency investment firm with more than $8 billion in assets.
Ehrsam graduated from Duke and worked as a foreign exchange trader at Goldman Sachs for two years before starting Coinbase.
Growing up, he played thousands of hours of World of Warcraft, where he first learned about the concept of in-game digital currencies.
